label: L=3 sequences, second copy step (recall_idx 1)
explanation: Fires at exactly one step: the second copy-phase step (t=4, outputting original token 1) of length-3 sequences, in essentially every L=3 sequence. It never fires on original-phase or delimiter steps, at any other step, or in sequences with L>=4. The token identities hardly change whether it fires. In the profile, magnitude was higher when the sequence had fewer digits, and many of the strongest examples had k among the original tokens. These magnitude trends were only seen in the profile tables and examples, not scored separately.

issues: Store mismatch with the user's request: the user asked to run the baseline on features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5. That directory holds only raw per-length .pt files (1M_128_high_seq3..9.pt), a subsample_manifest.json and a temp file. It is not a built autointerp store, so this check, like the original run, used features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store. These results are therefore for the full baseline store, not the 1/5 subsample the user asked for.

Minor: the magnitude trends (stronger when there are fewer digits, and 'k' showing up in top examples) come only from the profile and examples and were never scored. The explanation already says so, and they do not affect the predicate.
Minor: L=3 sequences make up only about 2.6% of sequences, so the unit fires on just 0.2% of steps. The label is accurate, but it describes a very narrow, position-only unit.
